text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
- ING Bank Romania managed a $160 million syndicated loan for fuel oil imports by the electricity authority Renel RA.
ADEVARUL
- The price of petrol is expected to rise to 1,800 lei per litre starting January, in line with a request from the National Oil Company.
- The Bucharest commodities exchange organises a tender on December 23 to sell 20,000 tonnes of scrap iron for the national railway company SNCFR.
ZIUA
- Branches of the savings bank CEC have so far approved 47.9 billion lei in credits for housing construction.
LIBERTATEA
- The new government wants to negotiate a new loan accord with the International Monetary Fund
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- Romania is expected to export 500,000 tonnes of maize in the first half of 1997.
General:
ROMANIA LIBERA

- The newspaper publishes the list of 27 members of the government of Prime Minister-designate Victor Ciorbea. The parliament meeting in a joint session on Wednesday is expected to discuss the list, as well as a governing programme.
- Police in the western town of Deva arrested three drug traffickers and seized 1.2 kg of cocaine.
ADEVARUL
- Foreigners found in Romania without a visa have to pay a one dollar fine according to a 1969 law which has not been revised.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- Each of the members of the new government must be sworn in by the President after getting a parliament approval.

- The newspaper carries extensive excerpts from former police chief General Ion Pitulescu's book on corruption in Romania, in which he details the case of miners' union leader Miron Cosma, who ousted the reformist government of Prime Minister Petre Roman in 1991.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- Ilie Verdet, leader of the Socialist Labour Party, said the governing programme of the centrist Democratic Convention (CDR) would push up inflation and trigger social unrest.
- The newspaper publishes a full-page report on the fate of abandoned and abused children in Romania. ($=3,618 lei) -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
